Find the arc length of the polar curve $r=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ for $\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{5\pi }{6}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above).
worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}1\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2\theta {|}_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6} \\  & =2(\frac{5\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
